mechanism_narrative: The continued decline in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT, together with rising RESIDENTIAL, signals weaker daytime circulation and fewer impulse purchases, so RETAIL_REC should keep falling over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days despite WORKPLACES staying below -5 and TRANSIT staying below -25 on weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL rises above 3 percent while TRANSIT remains below -25 percent, households substitute away from discretionary outings, causing RETAIL_REC to weaken within one to two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within 14 days after RESIDENTIAL exceeds 3 while TRANSIT stays below -25.

mechanism_narrative: A short-run rebound in GROCERY_PHARM reflects necessary errands, and if it keeps rising while RETAIL_REC stays negative, the errand channel spills into adjacent shopping trips and lifts RETAIL_REC over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve within 7 days after GROCERY_PHARM increases week on week.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility falls more than 3 points from one week to the next after a prior increase, discretionary outdoor activity is being displaced by caution, and retail visits weaken over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 3 points week-on-week after a prior weekly increase
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 28 days following a week-on-week PARKS drop greater than 3 points after an earlier rise.

mechanism_narrative: Under tightening restrictions, a simultaneous drop in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES reduces commuting-linked shopping and suppresses RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat over the next 14 days even though both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES decline for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in GROCERY_PHARM together with stable or rising RESIDENTIAL indicates more local, low-distance shopping patterns that partially support retail demand, so RETAIL_REC should improve over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains more negative over the next 28 days despite GROCERY_PHARM staying above 5 and RESIDENTIAL staying above 3.

mechanism_narrative: In a holiday-shopping regime, a week-over-week rise in PARKS is a proxy for leisure mobility and foot traffic, which should translate into higher RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS turns upward after being below -10
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 7 days after PARKS turns upward from below -10.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT stays below -28 while WORKPLACES does not recover above -6, the commuting network remains impaired and retail traffic continues to soften over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT below -28 and WORKPLACES below -6 for at least two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is higher over the next 28 days even though TRANSIT stays below -28 and WORKPLACES stays below -6 for two weeks.
